events.extended_summary: Representative-elect Anthony Constantino stated in a video that one of his goals is to get every gay American to be Republican. The 44-year-old sticker company owner narrowly won New York's 21st Congressional district in the 2026 midterms, defeating Democratic challenger Blake Gendebien 50.73 percent to 49.27 percent. Constantino claimed Democrats are not safe for the gay community and are willing to endanger their lives, while arguing the Republican Party offers low taxes, security, and safety. Exit polls showed only 12 percent of LGBTQ+ voters supported Republicans, while 86 percent voted for Kamala Harris in 2024. Data indicates 14.2 percent of Democrats identify as LGBTQ+ compared to 1.9 percent of Republicans. During his campaign, Constantino had accused a middle school teacher of grooming for supporting an LGBTQ+ club. The Republican Party spent an estimated $183 million on anti-transgender advertising during the midterms.
events.micro_summary: Representative-elect Anthony Constantino aims to make every gay American Republican after winning 50.73% of the vote.
events.summary: Representative-elect Anthony Constantino announced a goal to convert every gay American to the Republican Party after narrowly winning New York's 21st district with 50.73% of the vote, despite exit polls showing only 12% of LGBTQ+ voters supported Republicans.

events.extended_summary: The United States has launched another wave of sanctions against Iran under its Operation Economic Outcast, a move that comes shortly after US President Donald Trump threatened renewed military action next year. The Department of the Treasury announced on Monday that it had targeted more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies, and key personnel with sanctions “in a sweeping effort to disrupt Iran’s global shadow banking networks”. “Iran’s shadow banking system is the last financial lifeline of a bankrupt regime,” said US Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. The US Treasury claimed these entities help Iran “move billions of dollars through the international financial system to provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions”. Bessent also vowed the “Treasury will continue dismantling these illicit networks until we have buried the head of the snake.” The Central Bank of Iran oversees the designated entities, according to the
events.micro_summary: US escalates sanctions on Iran, targets ‘shadow banking’ networks.
events.summary: US escalates sanctions on Iran, targets ‘shadow banking’ networks. The US Treasury claimed these entities help Iran “move billions of dollars through the international financial system to provide the regime access to foreign currency despite comprehensive sanctions”.

events.extended_summary: A Ukrainian-made SPYS interceptor drone successfully destroyed a Russian Geran-5 K5-K during combat testing in Ukraine. Quantum WIY Industries confirmed the interception on November 23, stating the high-speed target was brought down without assistance from other air defense weapons. The Geran-5 K5-K, which Russia began deploying in early autumn, is classified by Ukrainian military intelligence as a compact cruise missile rather than a conventional drone. The weapon measures four meters in length with a three-meter wingspan, cruises above 450 km/h, can reach 1,000 km/h in maneuvers, operates at a ceiling of six kilometers, and has a range of 1,000 kilometers with a 90-kilogram thermobaric warhead. The SPYS interceptor, capable of speeds up to 450 kph and a four-kilometer ceiling, is designed to counter attack and reconnaissance drones to protect cities and critical infrastructure.
events.micro_summary: A Ukrainian SPYS interceptor drone destroyed a Russian Geran-5 K5-K cruise missile in combat testing.
events.summary: A Ukrainian SPYS interceptor drone shot down a Russian Geran-5 K5-K jet-powered drone on November 23, classified as a compact cruise missile, during combat testing without other air defense assistance.

events.extended_summary: As South Africa confronts another wave of gender-based violence and femicide, Mental Health Awareness Month should force us to ask what happens to the minds of women who survive, families who mourn, and communities learning to live with fear. South Africa has become dangerously familiar with the language of violence against women. Another woman is killed, another family waits for answers, another name is added to a growing list, and another national conversation begins. Yet when the headlines disappear, the consequences remain. For the women who survive violence, the families left behind, and communities forced to confront these crimes, there is no simple return to normal. There is fear, grief, anger, and anxiety about who could be next. This is why the country's gender-based violence and femicide (GBVF) crisis must also be understood as a mental-health crisis. The recent killings in Ekurhuleni have once again placed the issue firmly in
events.micro_summary: South Africa femicide: Night-time curfews and street patrols after women murdered in Ekurhuleni.

events.extended_summary: President Trump granted a "full, absolute and unconditional pardon" to two turkeys named Freedom and Feathers during a ceremony in Washington, announcing that future pardon ceremonies will be held at the new White House ballroom. The president described the 90,000 sq ft ballroom, being constructed on the site of the former East Wing, as "missile-proof, drone-proof, bullet-proof" and said it will host state functions. The turkeys, whose names were selected by public vote and who weigh a combined 82 pounds, spent the previous night at the Willard Hotel. Raised in West Virginia, both birds will live out their days at Texas A&M following the ceremony. Trump joked that the pardon meant the turkeys "will live forever" and noted that traditionally only one turkey attends the ceremony.
events.micro_summary: President Trump pardoned turkeys Freedom and Feathers and announced future pardons at the new ballroom.
events.summary: President Trump granted a full pardon to turkeys Freedom and Feathers in Washington and announced next year's ceremony will move to the new 90,000 sq ft missile-proof White House ballroom.

events.extended_summary: Huawei Technologies was found guilty of 10 out of 12 counts in a Brooklyn federal court trial, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank fraud, and conspiracy to violate US sanctions, but was acquitted of the racketeering conspiracy charge. The two-month trial followed charges announced in 2019, after senior executive Meng Wanzhou's 2018 arrest in Canada and subsequent three-year detention before her release through a deal with US prosecutors. Prosecutors alleged Huawei spent 20 years lying to banks about Iran dealings and stealing technology from rivals, while the defence argued the company's success in 170 countries with over 200,000 staff resulted from innovation and hard work rather than criminal enterprise. US Attorney General Todd Blanche stated the verdict holds accountable those who engaged in criminal activities, while defence attorney Brian Heberlig welcomed the rejection of the racketeering charge.
events.micro_summary: Huawei found guilty of 10 of 12 counts but acquitted of racketeering conspiracy charge.
events.summary: Huawei was found guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but acquitted of the racketeering charge in a Brooklyn federal court trial.

events.extended_summary: The United States is preparing to announce new tariffs on 16 jurisdictions, including China, the European Union, Mexico and Japan, following a Section 301 investigation launched in March after the Supreme Court ruled President Trump's Liberation Day tariffs illegal. Countries will face different import tax rates depending on deals previously struck with the administration. The move is expected to increase tensions between the US and China, whose interim trade agreement expires on January 10. Washington has accused Beijing of failing to meet commitments from October 2025 regarding agricultural purchases, rare earths and critical minerals, though China extended the suspension of an export ban on gallium, germanium and antimony until January 27. The tariffs represent a continuation of Trump's signature trade policy aimed at boosting American manufacturing, following sweeping tariffs unveiled in April 2025 that were later struck down.
events.micro_summary: The US is preparing to announce new tariffs on 16 jurisdictions including China, the EU, Mexico and Japan.
events.summary: The US is preparing to announce new tariffs on 16 jurisdictions including China, the European Union, Mexico and Japan following a Section 301 investigation, with rates varying by previous deals and an interim US-China agreement set to expire January 10.

events.extended_summary: The recent failure of the UN climate summit COP31 exceeded already gloomy expectations, creating a political and diplomatic catastrophe that may serve as a historical opportunity to address structural problems in global climate governance. For 31 years, the COP process has required unanimous consensus from all 195 nations or parties to make decisions, a rule stemming from draft rule 42 of the Framework Convention on Climate Change that was never formally accepted or rejected. This unanimity trap was demonstrated in 2010 when Bolivia alone objected and risked derailing negotiations. While the process produced the 2015 Paris agreement, reformers argue that unanimity must be abolished in favor of a two-thirds majority system used by the UN General Assembly, UNESCO, and the World Health Organization. Additionally, the COP remains inefficient and exclusionary, including tiny nations like San Marino while omitting megacities such as Mumbai and Seattle that face significant climate risks.
events.micro_summary: COP31 failed catastrophically, prompting urgent calls to abolish the unanimity rule that has trapped climate talks for 31 years.
events.summary: The failed COP31 climate summit has intensified demands to reform the UN process by abolishing the unanimity requirement that has governed 195 nations for 31 years, replacing it with a two-thirds majority voting system used by other UN bodies.

events.extended_summary: Ukrainian forces may have struck a Russian military surveillance facility in the Smolensk region on November 21. The target was the AP-MRIK-VKO multifunctional aerospace defense information complex, operated by Russia's 572nd Separate Radio-Technical Unit and associated with the 821st Main Center for Space Situation Reconnaissance. Located in the Mityuli region, the facility houses 80P6 radar systems deployed in 2021 to collect and process intelligence on atmospheric and outer space activity supporting Russian air and missile defense. Preliminary reports indicate Ukrainian forces deployed more than 30 jet-powered drones during the operation, potentially damaging both the radar installation and the radio-technical unit's headquarters, though the full extent of destruction has not been confirmed.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian forces struck a Russian aerospace surveillance facility in Smolensk on November 21, damaging radar equipment.
events.summary: Ukrainian drones may have struck a Russian military surveillance facility in the Smolensk region on November 21, potentially damaging radar equipment and headquarters at the AP-MRIK-VKO complex.

events.extended_summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Senegal are the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, overturning a Confederation of African Football appeal board decision that had stripped them of the title. Senegal defeated host nation Morocco 1-0 in the January final in Rabat, with Pape Gueye scoring the winner in extra time after Brahim Diaz missed a penalty. The match was delayed over 15 minutes when Senegal players walked off in protest at a late penalty award. A CAF panel had initially awarded Morocco a 3-0 win for the walk-off, but CAS reinstated the original result, stating the referee's decision to resume play fell within his sole authority. The three-man CAS panel heard the case in Lausanne on 8 October and issued a unanimous verdict confirming the 1-0 result. Morocco's football federation expressed astonishment and said it would pursue all available legal procedures to appeal.
events.micro_summary: Court of Arbitration for Sport confirms Senegal as 2025 AFCON winners with 1-0 final result reinstated.
events.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has confirmed Senegal as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners, overturning a decision that stripped them of the title after they beat Morocco 1-0 in the January final.

events.extended_summary: Manchester City secured a 2-2 draw against Napoli at home in the Champions League, with Rayan Cherki scoring a late equalizer to salvage a point. Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund opened the scoring for the Italian side in the second half, before Ayyoub Bouaddi netted his first goal for the club to level the match. Noa Lang restored Napoli's lead on 76 minutes with a volley from Leonardo Spinazzola's cross, but Cherki drilled low into the bottom corner late on to rescue the draw. The result leaves City in sixth place in the Champions League table, though they are likely to drop out of the top eight by Wednesday. The club has now gone 10 games without a clean sheet and has won just one of their past seven matches in all competitions under manager Enzo Maresca.
events.micro_summary: Rayan Cherki's late goal earned Manchester City a 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League.
events.summary: Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli at the Etihad Stadium in the Champions League after Rayan Cherki's late strike cancelled out Noa Lang's volley, leaving City sixth in the table and without a clean sheet in 10 games.

events.extended_summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 204 off 53 balls for India A against the United Arab Emirates in the Asia Cup Rising Stars competition, setting multiple List A records. The 15-year-old reached his century in 28 balls, his 150 in 40 balls, and his double century in 52 balls, breaking previous records of 29, 59, and 103 balls respectively. He also hit 28 sixes during his innings, surpassing the previous record of 23. India chased down the target of 250 set by the UAE to finish at 3-254, with more than 80 percent of the team's runs coming from Sooryavanshi's bat. He also holds the fastest List A half-century record, reaching 50 off 11 balls earlier in 2026.
events.micro_summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 204 off 53 balls to set fastest List A century and double century records.

sources.publisher: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

events.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 204 off 53 balls against UAE, setting List A records for fastest century (28 balls), 150 (40), and double century (52), while hitting 28 sixes as India chased 250 to finish 3-254.

events.extended_summary: Torrential rainfall across Gaza has caused severe flooding, displacing tens of thousands of people and flooding more than 70,000 tents in just 12 hours. Displaced residents describe the conditions as horrific, with many left drenched and without shelter. Meanwhile, 150,000 tents and other vital winter supplies remain blocked at the border, prevented from entering the enclave. Britain, Canada, Australia and Italy have jointly demanded that Israel lift restrictions on these critical relief supplies before winter fully sets in. Israeli authorities claim that over 93,000 tents and more than 8,600 trucks carrying winter supplies have already entered Gaza, while humanitarian organisations argue that civilian suffering is being prolonged by border decisions, with children sleeping in floodwater while shelter kits wait at the borders.
events.micro_summary: Severe flooding has displaced tens of thousands in Gaza as 150,000 tents remain blocked at the border.
events.summary: Torrential rain has flooded over 70,000 tents in Gaza, displacing tens of thousands, while 150,000 winter tents and vital supplies remain blocked at the border despite demands from Britain, Canada, Australia and Italy for Israel to lift restrictions.

events.extended_summary: At least 11 people were wounded following a drone attack by Yemen's Houthi group on a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District on Tuesday. The injured included two Saudi citizens, two Indian nationals, three Nepali nationals and four Egyptian nationals. Emergency services responded immediately to protect civilian lives and property. The targeted building houses the headquarters of the Saudi Public Investment Fund and is the country's tallest skyscraper, with images showing damage about halfway up the facade. The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government described the attack as cowardly and targeting civilians, vowing a firm response. The Houthi group, which controls much of western Yemen including Sanaa, has been firing at Saudi targets since Yemen's frozen civil war reignited in July. The Gulf Cooperation Council secretary-general condemned the attack as a heinous crime and aggression, calling for a decisive international stance to hold the militia accountable.
events.micro_summary: At least 11 people were wounded in a Houthi drone attack on a Riyadh financial district tower.
events.summary: At least 11 people were wounded when Yemen's Houthi group launched a drone attack on a Riyadh financial district tower, injuring two Saudis, two Indians, three Nepalis and four Egyptians and damaging the facade of the country's tallest skyscraper.

Rosstat's documents alone cannot capture the full
events.micro_summary: At least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine, data leak reveals.

events.extended_summary: The UK government has issued a security alert warning that businesses supplying the Ukrainian Armed Forces are being targeted by the Russian state, prompting closed-door threat briefings for critical national infrastructure and defence sector CEOs in Whitehall. The National Protective Security Agency, part of MI5, warned of increased sabotage risks including arson and threats to staff, citing recent incidents such as a September court case involving plans to torch UK drone factories, an attempted arson at an Estonian drone factory, and a drone attack at Leipzig airport in August. Defence and security ministers alongside intelligence representatives will chair briefings on Tuesday and Wednesday to provide tailored security advice, urging organisations to reduce digital exposure, install visible protective measures such as CCTV and secure entrances, and ensure staff remain alert to hostile reconnaissance. The Security Minister described the targeting of organisations supporting Ukraine as "truly shameful."
events.micro_summary: UK warns businesses supporting Ukraine of Russian sabotage threats and convenes closed-door security briefings for defence CEOs.
events.summary: UK intelligence warns businesses supplying Ukraine's armed forces are being targeted by Russia and convenes closed-door briefings for critical infrastructure and defence CEOs to strengthen protections against sabotage.

events.extended_summary: At the fifth India International Space Conclave 2026 in New Delhi, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh announced that India's space economy, currently valued at nearly $9 billion, is projected to expand to $40-45 billion in less than a decade, driven by private investment and indigenous development. He noted the space ecosystem has grown from a handful of startups to nearly 400-500 companies, reflecting reforms under Prime Minister Narendra Modi that opened the sector to private participation through NewSpace India Limited and IN-SPACe. Singh highlighted Skyroot's maiden launch on July 18, 2026, and its unicorn status, alongside Agnikul and others developing propulsion systems and rocket engines. He emphasized space technology's value extends beyond launches to improving efficiency across sectors, citing the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan.
events.micro_summary: Dr. Jitendra Singh said India's $9 billion space economy will reach $40-45 billion within a decade at the 2026 conclave.
events.summary: At the fifth India International Space Conclave 2026 in New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh stated India's space economy, valued at nearly $9 billion, will grow to $40-45 billion in under a decade, with the ecosystem expanding to 400-500 companies.

events.extended_summary: "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend" has become the highest-grossing Indian film of all time in international markets outside China, collecting $59 million (approximately Rs 490 crore) overseas and surpassing "Dhurandhar: The Revenge," which previously held the record with $51 million. North America emerged as the biggest market with $28.4 million across the US and Canada. The film also set all-time records for Indian releases in Thailand ($1.9 million), Nepal ($1.5 million), Indonesia ($1.2 million), the Netherlands ($610,000), and Cambodia ($355,000). Other major markets include the UK ($6.5 million), UAE ($5.4 million), Australia ($5.1 million), Malaysia ($1.7 million), and Germany ($1.2 million). Worldwide, the film has reached $147.5 million, ranking fifth among highest-grossing Indian films globally. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash, the $200 million production is scheduled for releases in China, Japan, and South Korea, with a sequel planned for 2028.
events.micro_summary: "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend" becomes highest-grossing Indian film internationally with $59 million overseas earnings.
events.summary: "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend" has surpassed "Dhurandhar: The Revenge" to become the highest-grossing Indian film in international markets, earning $59 million overseas, with North America contributing $28.4 million.

events.extended_summary: Yash has become the first Indian actor to have two releases cross ₹50 crore across all five major Indian languages—Hindi, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, and Malayalam—after Ramayana achieved the feat 19 days into its run. He previously accomplished this with KGF: Chapter 2, which earned ₹487.56 crore in Hindi, ₹170.77 crore in Kannada, ₹132.02 crore in Telugu, ₹114.94 crore in Tamil, and ₹55.94 crore in Malayalam. Ramayana, in which Yash portrays Ravana and serves as producer, has crossed ₹50 crore gross in each language for an all-India gross of ₹1,141 crore. The film has reached ₹1,709 crore worldwide, with domestic collections at ₹1,141 crore gross across 4,12,560 shows and overseas markets contributing ₹568.00 crore. Ramayana also surpassed Dhurandhar: The Revenge in the US with $28.4 million, and Yash now has two films crossing ₹1,000 crore globally, with a combined tally exceeding ₹3,000 crore.
events.micro_summary: Yash becomes first Indian actor with two films crossing ₹50 crore in all five major Indian languages.
events.summary: Yash becomes the first Indian actor to have two films cross ₹50 crore in Hindi, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam, after Ramayana joined KGF: Chapter 2 in achieving the milestone with ₹1,141 crore domestic gross.

events.extended_summary: QNu Labs, a provider of hybrid quantum cybersecurity solutions, signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT), an autonomous scientific society under India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, to strengthen quantum technology education and capacity building in India. The collaboration will develop learning and training programmes in quantum technologies, including quantum-safe cybersecurity, and establish Quantum Labs at mutually identified institutions through a Hub-and-Spoke model. The partnership will create industry-oriented curricula, learning resources, and practical training opportunities, including hands-on demonstrations, projects, hackathons, faculty development, Train-the-Trainer programmes, assessment and certification, as well as internships and on-the-job training. The initiative aims to bridge the gap between emerging technology requirements and industry-ready skills by combining QNu Labs' quantum technology experience with NIELIT's institutional network and technical education expertise.
events.micro_summary: QNu Labs and NIELIT signed an MoU to expand quantum technology education and workforce training in India.
events.summary: QNu Labs signed a Memorandum of Understanding with NIELIT to develop quantum technology curricula, establish Quantum Labs via a Hub-and-Spoke model, and provide hands-on training, certification, and industry placements in quantum-safe cybersecurity across India.

events.extended_summary: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 204 off 53 balls with 28 sixes and seven fours as India A defeated the United Arab Emirates by seven wickets in an ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup match in Doha. Chasing UAE's 8-249 from 50 overs, India A reached 3-254 with 35.4 overs to spare. Sooryavanshi set List A records for the fastest century, beating Jake Fraser-McGurk's 29-ball mark by one delivery, and the fastest double century with a 52-ball 200, nearly twice as fast as the previous 103-ball mark. His 28 sixes broke D'Arcy Short's record of 23 maximums. He became India's youngest men's international in July with his T20 debut against England, surpassing Sachin Tendulkar's record. He previously scored 175 in the Under-19 World Cup final in February and hit a 35-ball century in the Indian Premier League last year, finishing as the tournament's leading run-scorer with 72 sixes this season.
events.micro_summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 204 off 53 balls with 28 sixes as India A beat UAE by seven wickets.
events.summary: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off 53 balls with 28 sixes as India A chased down UAE's 8-249 to win by seven wickets with 35.4 overs to spare in Doha, setting List A records for fastest century and double century.

events.extended_summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 204 off 53 balls for India A against the UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars at the University of Doha for Science and Technology, breaking multiple List A world records. He reached his century in 28 balls, the fastest in List A history, surpassing the previous 29-ball record, and his double-century in 52 balls, nearly halving Chad Bowes' 103-ball mark. He also hit 28 sixes, the most in a List A innings, and reached 150 off 40 balls. Caught at long-off by Basil Hameed in the 13th over with his side five runs short of the target, Sooryavanshi struck at 384.90 with seven fours. India A chased down 250 in 14.2 overs, winning by seven wickets with 214 balls remaining after Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma opened with 68 runs in 21 balls.
events.micro_summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 204 off 53 balls to break multiple List A records against UAE.
events.summary: India A's Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit 204 off 53 balls against UAE, breaking world records for fastest List A century (28 balls), 150 (40), and double-century (52), while hitting 28 sixes as India A won by seven wickets chasing 250.

events.extended_summary: Thirteen people were killed and 14 others injured when a passenger bus carrying 41 people collided with a truck on Al Watan Road in Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates. The truck had stopped on the roadside due to a mechanical fault. The death toll initially stood at 11 but rose to 13 after two victims succumbed to injuries in hospital. Indian nationals were among the deceased, prompting the Indian Consulate in Dubai to reach out to bereaved families and offer assistance through a 24-hour toll-free helpline, 800-46342. Emergency response teams, ambulance crews, and civil defence conducted rescue operations at the scene. The UAE Ministry of Interior launched an investigation into the causes. The incident occurred days after a separate multi-vehicle accident in Fujairah on November 12 that killed 14 people and injured 30, including four Indian nationals.
events.micro_summary: Thirteen people were killed in a bus-truck collision in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE, including Indian nationals.
events.summary: Thirteen people were killed and 14 injured when a passenger bus collided with a truck on Al Watan Road in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE. Indian nationals were among the deceased, and the Indian Consulate in Dubai is assisting families.

events.extended_summary: India announced a $1.62 billion package of grants and credit for reconstruction, infrastructure and energy for Nepal following devastating floods in August that rank among the country's worst recorded disasters. New Delhi was the first foreign government to respond, sending relief supplies and helping restore communications. The aid was extended during Prime Minister Balendra Shah's first bilateral visit to India since taking power in March. Nepal requires approximately $5 billion to rebuild damaged infrastructure, and India's package represents the largest financial assistance the nation has ever received. Indian aid disbursement to Nepal exceeded China's by more than fourfold in the 2024-25 fiscal year. The move comes as relations between the neighbors had frayed over border disputes and resentment regarding a 2015 blockade, while China expanded its trade and infrastructure influence in the landlocked Himalayan nation.
events.micro_summary: India pledged $1.62 billion in aid to flood-hit Nepal during Prime Minister Shah's visit.
events.summary: India announced a $1.62 billion reconstruction package for flood-devastated Nepal during Prime Minister Balendra Shah's first visit to New Delhi, the largest aid Nepal has received, as New Delhi seeks to rebuild influence amid strained ties.

events.extended_summary: At least six people were killed and 10 others injured after a powerful explosion ripped through a restaurant on Nguyen Van Tuyet Street in Hanoi's Dong Da district on Tuesday around 8 am. Police suspect a gas leak caused the blast. The explosion partially collapsed the building and damaged around 10 neighboring houses within a 15-metre radius, scattering debris across more than 20 metres of road. Ten injured people received treatment at Saint Paul General Hospital, Dong Da General Hospital, and Hanoi Medical University Hospital. One victim died at Dong Da General Hospital after being struck by flying debris while walking past. Rescue teams used detection equipment and hydraulic machinery to search rubble for survivors, while residents helped pull bodies from the debris. Authorities feared more people could be trapped as the restaurant was open during the blast.
events.micro_summary: At least six people were killed and 10 injured in a suspected gas explosion at a Hanoi restaurant.
events.summary: At least six people were killed and 10 injured when a suspected gas leak caused an explosion at a restaurant in Hanoi's Dong Da district on Tuesday morning, partially collapsing the building and damaging nearby houses.
